title: 8-minute outage during a database migration deploy
body: A deploy shipping a schema migration (moving event embeddings to a side table, part of a database cost-reduction effort) stalled at boot: the migration's CREATE INDEX statement blocked on a lock held by a concurrent index build still running from the pre-deploy backfill. Health checks failed and the edge refused traffic until the conflicting index build was terminated, letting the migration and boot complete. Lesson recorded: never ship a migration touching a table while a concurrent index build on it is still running — sequence them.

title: Brief outage: machine OOM-killed, auto-restarted
body: Same root cause as 2026-08-05: the feed-crawler memory leak hit the 512MB ceiling. The machine restarted cleanly this time (~1 min blip). Root cause was identified and fixed the same day: the RSS fetch path leaked a socket + response buffer for every dead feed on every crawl cycle (~16MB per 10-minute cycle). Feeds are now fetched with hard-abort timeouts; memory is flat. Postmortem: https://github.com/zatmonkey/newsflash-status#2026-08-06

title: Outage: OOM-killed process restarted into a wedged state
body: The app process was OOM-killed at 04:06 PT (memory leak in the feed crawler, later fixed). The auto-restarted process came back wedged — health checks timed out and Fly's edge refused all traffic. Recovered by a manual machine restart. Follow-ups shipped: swap enabled, automatic restart on sustained health failure (this probe), and the leak itself fixed on 2026-08-06.
